note: Kept for next session; nothing ruled, LP60 stands as one centre between the seats (tentative). First play, every figure a guess until V-109, V-110 and a seated ear position are measured (ear 330 mm off the centreline, 180 below the headliner). 1. Both centres on the car's centreline means the driver and the passenger sit mirror-image to the pair, so one delay on the roof speaker lines the two up for both seats at once - the one two-speaker layout in a car where that is true. That, not a polarity flip, is the cure for the combing (a flip only moves the nulls); it needs the roof centre on its own DSP channel. 2. Where along the car the pair sits matters more than anything else. At the seat line (roof over the console, low between the seats): paths 376 and 599 mm, 0.65 ms apart, first null 770 Hz untreated, and the voice is 90 degrees to the side - at your shoulder. Slid forward to the windshield header and the dash or console front (550 to 750 mm ahead of the ears): 0.34 to 0.41 ms apart, the voice 25 to 31 degrees inboard of straight ahead, and once delayed a 50 mm change in ear height puts the first null at 4 to 5.5 kHz instead of 2.6 kHz. So: a high centre at the header and a low centre at the dash centre, not a pair between the shoulders. 3. Level and band are then the upmix's dials (D-503, ours to write): the low one carries the voice's body, the roof one lifts the image; how much and from what frequency is tuning by ear with the firmware, not a parts choice. What it would touch if ruled: LP60 becomes two matched small coaxials; LP57 needs 7 processed channels, so an 8-channel DSP-amp (noted on X-012 so the round does not pick a 6-channel one); a second speaker pair up the A-pillar and a housing beside L3-CTR in electrical; a shallow driver and a pod at the header against the roof skin and headliner (PT916, PT774) - depth there is the unknown that decides it; the dash centre gets a speaker opening (04-beauty and the dash CAD).
